en: O Ocean of aquatic creatures, whose form is as vast as the earth, whose waters are agitated by the spitting of the serpent Śeṣa,
within whose depths the flood of all activities is contained, you who are praised by the Supreme Lord (Brahmā),

you who are desired by the Knower of Self (Viṣṇu), and who are beloved by the Sun’s son (Yama)— at the time of the end of the age, for the sake of the purpose of non-activity, you have descended into this lower state.
O Lord whose excellent body possesses the luster of a golden mountain, who carries the clouds upon the horns of Your most steadfast self!

O Lord, whose golden tusk-vessel today is made exceedingly fierce by the expansion of abundant, breaking foam like thick curd; O You of most wonderful gait, intoxicated by Your power; O You of immeasurable deeds, fierce as a horse;

O You who are an elephant-trunk to the pride of the throats of wicked ones; O You who create the destruction of the demon Khaṇḍa with Your arm; O You who have the face of the horse of the Lord of the Gods—grant me Your unbroken and stainless vision. || 2 ||

May he who is in the form of a tortoise protect you; may he whose nature is playfulness protect you; may he who bore Mount Mandara upon his back protect you; may he who is the support of Dharma protect you; may he who is ever possessed of the bliss of the Sudharmā assembly hall protect you; may he who, by bestowing nectar, is skilled in piercing the vital organs of the deceitful demon Rāhu, the embodiment of evil pride, protect you.
O Lord, you possess the splendor of the sun of Dharma and excellent armor; you are free from all distortions in the creation of the world. || 3 ||

O Dhanvantari, whose limbs possess a radiant luster; O Dhanvantari, who are the tree that destroys enemies; O you who dwell within the sun, the nectar of the earth, and the interval between the ages (Manvantara); O sovereign of the Manvantaras, O treasure-house of medicines that extend across the world; O you who dispel the pain of the body of Danu’s son (the demon Jambha) in battles; O you who expand the ocean of my [joy] like a son to your daughter (Lakṣmī); O you whose bodily parts are as vast as the end-maker (Death) himself; [protect me] in the ocean of internal suffering. 1. O you who dispel the pain of the body of Danu’s son (the demon Jambha

May she whose body is green protect you—she who was born from the churning of the ocean of milk for the sake of the gods’ hope against the demons of undiminished pride; she whose face is veiled by sharp locks of hair that surpass the orb of the moon, who casts aside her fine lower garment, and who, with side-glances that humble the penance of the mind, has seized the nectar from the gods by her harsh gaze.
The daughter of Daksha (Dakshayani), who is capable of examining the auspicious marks of initiation and is devoted to the rules of discipline and conduct,
forgives even the direct insults of Rama;
she whose feet, stained with the lac-dye that captivates the eyes of those who gaze at her, mark the earth as they step forward.
May she, whose body is directly manifested, who bestows the earth, and who possesses the eye upon her forehead that is capable [of all things], protect us. || 6 ||

Obeisance to You, who possess the splendor of a dark blue cloud; who bear a body as majestic as a mountain of virtuous conduct; who are joined with the playful ocean, the river of curds, the mountains, and all else; who are the fire that consumes the forest of cotton that is the host of asuras upon the entire earth; who take the form of a boar; who are the support for the ocean and the Black Mountain (Kālācala); who bear fangs like blue lotuses; whose broad feet are the playground for the Earth; who are the supreme root of bliss for the assembly of yogins; and who are saluted by the multitude of sages. 7.

O Nṛhari, whose sharp talons are like thunderbolts that split the frontal globes of the lordly elephant—the enemy of Indra; who, as a young elephant, was granted a boon to a child suffering from consumption; whose roar is profound; and who is the lotus-born Brahmā, the Wind-god, the Earth, the elephant-headed Gaṇeśa, the lord of serpents, and the king of birds, following the Goddess born from the ocean—protect me with compassion!
O wearer of the skin of the lord of elephants, O enemy of Jambha, you who are praised by the lotus-like faces of the six-faced one (Kārttikeya), protect me! 8.

O Piṅgākṣa, O Vāmana, whose fourfold army of horses and other forces displayed its prowess; you who gladdened the limbs of Bali—the haughty lord of the Danujas—standing at the sacrifice as he fell along with his entire retinue; you who were praised by the swan-like gods;

you whose lofty tips of toenails, adorned with beauty, pierced the golden mountain peak; you who were overwhelmed by the exceedingly auspicious waves of the river falling from that peak; O Vāmana, destroy the sins of my limbs; salutations to you! 9.

O Lord of the dwarf body, worthy of meditation, protect the sacrificer! You who, for the sake of bestowing the earth upon the Lord of the Gods, acted as a petitioner; you who subdued various members of the assembly and the demons through the power of your speech;
you whose own form was equal to ten million spotless moons; you who held in your hands the sacred girdle, the loincloth, the clear thread, the sandals, the parasol, and the excellent staff.

O ocean of fortitude, O sovereign who has severed the foremost of the wicked with the axe of your conduct, O you whose mass of pride in the strength of your arms was surpassed by the great heroism born in the son of Kṛtavīrya, O you whose noble sons were sacrificed when they fell from their manliness due to the command of an Ārya angered by the offense of your wife—
may your immeasurable heroism, which conquers the multitude of noble ones, show compassion toward me, regardless of my own transgression. 11.

O Śrī Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, Parrot-Rāma, Bhūrava, Gaura, Amala, Amita, Mahāhāra, and you whose fame is praised by the gods; O son of Rāma’s splendor, O remover of the desires of the godless, O best among those who find delight in themselves, O enemy of the army of heroes, O you whose hips are covered with bark-garments as pure as fine raiment, O you who are a garden of bliss, O you who have attained a most terrible yet beautiful victory over the demon Māra! 12.

O Keśava, who bestows glory; O Lord of the world, whose hair is like the dawn; O sole remover of the suffering of others when the sun of their fortune has set; O cloud to the peacock of those whose intellects find happiness in absolute bliss;

O Lord of Sāketa, chief among those with excellent feet; O Hṛṣīkeśa, whose face is like the orb of the full moon and whose glance removes the pain of the crow—[I offer] incomparable devotion at Your lotus feet. 13.

O Rāma, who are delightful to the hearts of men, terrifying to the hosts of enemies, and who conquered the earth; O Śyāma, whose mind is fixed on the immeasurable ascetic Gādhisuta (Viśvāmitra), and who have forever surpassed all others in victory over immeasurable austerities— may my mind today find delight in you.
O victorious one, who has conquered the fair-eyed goddess with immeasurable heroism by shattering the bow of Bhīma! || 14 ||
O you whose face resounds like a cuckoo in the forest of the beloved’s home, who possess arrows that are the tormentors of lovely tresses,
who are the moon to the lineage of the lovely-eyed one, and who destroy the splendor of the lovely gems and the like—
follow me, O Lord, who are adorned with lovely tilakas and whose locks of hair are as lovely as trembling petals.
May she, who was victorious over the difficult forest camps by following her beloved, protect me, O Ramā! 15.
Worship with devotion that Lord who is self-subdued, the end of the son of Daśānana, who dwells upon the earth,
who has reached the edge of the forest exhausted by fierce penance, who is the infinite Yama to the multitude of ascetics,
and who goes to the end of the fear of worldly existence for me; do so quickly and with great intensity.
He was the end of his own mind, the end of the demons including Vārida, the end of the night for the mountains, and the best among ascetics.
O you whose immeasurable fame was established by the destruction of the enemy forces with the lightning-like tremors of your hand,

O you who bring auspiciousness, may you— by the essence of your compassion— fully protect me; for you purified the wing of Sampāti, born together with him, which had been struck down by the sinner Rāvaṇa, as it fell at your lotus-feet.
Protect me, who have fallen into a well of evil, even though you dwell upon the banks of Lake Pampā. 17.

O you whose gait is full of curiosity for the sport of slaying the deer of graceful movements watched by the tremulous-eyed one; O protector of the younger brother who was carried off from the place of conversation by a young girl; O you who are like the wind to the house of the city burnt by the fire of Bālā; O you who have attained the dust of the surface of the earth through the power of your plow! Victory, victory to you!
From the ocean that lies beyond the path of the bees formed by the rows of monkeys beginning with Nīla and Aṅgada.

Victorious is the son of the Lord of Speech (Brahmā), whose arms and hands bear the scars of quivers, bows, and swords; whose incomparable luster is like a mass of clouds; who protects his face and nose which resemble a mountain range; whose corners of the eyes turn crimson; whose feet are covered by rows of jewels offered as worship by the lords of the oceans; and who is praised here by the excellent speech of Bāṇa.

The sound of his bow— preceded by the syllable *huṃ* and followed by the roar of the *ṭaṅkāra*, which was perceived as moving through the thick mud of the earth and causing the mountains of Laṅkā to tremble with fear— filled the Lord of Laṅkā with terror; with a mind agitated by hundreds of doubts, he regarded it as the Night of Doom itself.
Worship that Hari, who bears the marks of the bow and arrows resembling hundreds of the staff of Death.

Hari—who possesses the splendor of immeasurable intellect, whose name brings auspiciousness to those afflicted by distress, whose greatness is worshipped by Lakṣmī, Brahmā, Śiva, the gods, serpents, and the enemy of the serpent-king (Garuḍa), as well as by the Moon and others;

who is the limit of stability and other virtues, who destroyed Rāvaṇa along with his entire host, who is the slayer of Rāma (Paraśurāma), who assumes forms beyond the earth (such as the Fish and Tortoise), and who is the subject of the Vedas beginning with the Sāman—[is the Lord]. || 21 ||
By the word of his lord, who was of a nature prone to faults due to the transgression of the month of Āṣāḍha,
he whose feet were wandering to give garments and ornaments to the wives of sages who had become like stone,
and who brought auspiciousness by punishing those who committed evil deeds against women of the Niṣādas.
May He, who removes defects, birth, death, and emaciation, protect us by destroying those born from the feet of Sudosā. 22.

We bow down to the son of Nanda, who is the forest for the herds of cattle dwelling in Vṛndāvana, the sole refuge of the gods who offer praise, the slayer of the Asuras who committed insults, whose belly is bound with a rope,
and whose face puts to shame even the beauty of the moon.
Whose teeth are like jasmine buds, whose body is white as a kunda flower, and who is the destroyer of the Dāva Rākṣasa.

O You who took away the Parijata tree from the cowherds, protect us from various calamities—You who were provoked by the cowherds' anger at the disappearance of the food, soups, and savory delicacies prepared for their festival; You who caused the mountain to be held up by the waters of the cloud-line when it was threatened by the curse of the cowherd women; and You who were intent on the task of stealing the garments of the cowherd women, whose bodies were colored with unguents and who suffered the heat born from the glance of Your sidelong glances.

Alas, I devotedly worship that multitude of virtuous souls who have attained birth as sons of kings—such as Kaṃsa and others—who were ornaments of wickedness; who, though born in this world of transmigration, have minds bound by worldly existence yet possess bodies of bliss through essential consciousness; and who incessantly bring about the ultimate perfection of those very beings.
The abode of the desire for liberation for sages such as Haṃsa, whose feet are to be venerated by those such as the Paramahaṃsas. || 25 ||

O lotus-eyed one, O Vidura, may you protect me; you who are under the sway of the one whose banner is the lotus; you who subdue the pride of the multitudes of kings accompanied by horses, elephants, foot-soldiers, and chariots;
O Lord of horses, O Lord of white steeds, O you whose arms shatter the bodies of the lords of the Daityas.
His head was exquisitely perfumed with jājī, kadamba, nava-rājīva, and other excellent sumana flowers.

Victory, victory to You, whose toenails are established upon Kālī, the abode of the heart; who possess the luster of a dark female serpent reddened by the multitude of sword-blades that are Your outstretched arms; O You whose heart is marked by particles of the saffron dust from the bodies of the cowherd women—the crest-jewels of the earth—who were arrogant due to the boons granted by Kālīśa, yet were stripped of their pride through Your playful pastimes! 27.

O Unconquered One, O Hari, who delights in the embrace of the dark-complexioned Draupadī— the daughter of Pāṇḍu who was filled with intense longing for Kṛṣṇa— O Dispeller of the sins called "Kṛṣṇa," O Lord of the six great heroines beginning with Kṛṣṇā; may You, whose face is like the orb of the cool-rayed moon, nourish me, O Master who has reached the further shore of the ocean of knowledge!
O Victorious One, O Supporter of the Lord of Mountains, O Viṣṇu, O Youngest Brother of Vṛṣa, O Bold One—may you [protect us] with compassion. || 28 ||

O Mādhava, O destroyer of the demon Vyoma, O son of Maratā, grant me delight in Your lotus feet— You who wear the crest-jewel of Rāmā (Lakṣmī), who are accompanied by Balarāma and His younger brother (Subhadrā),
and whose slender form captivates the hearts of the beautiful-eyed women of Bhūmipura who are afflicted by love for You.
O Lord whose face is praised by the celestial beings led by Bhīma and Ahi, O you whose feet are venerated by Bhīma! || 29 ||
The direct experience of the tossing of water and the binding with nooses by the hosts of Dākṣiśravas who were terrified by the consumption of food mixed with poison;
the former calamities such as the fire in the lacquer house, the Rākṣasa, Hiḍimba, Baka, and the lack of alms-food;
and the hearing of harsh words resulting from the addiction to dice and the state of existence—[all these] were vomited forth by the Great Queen.
Frequenting the inner apartments, serving base kings, and constant derision of the wicked. || 30 ||

Victorious is the Lord of Lakṣmī, the King of the Yadus, who, while observing his own side consisting of the sons of the thousand-eyed Indra and other friends, had his mind consecrated for the agitation caused by the power of hundreds of Akṣauhiṇīs belonging to wicked kings who challenged him;
disregarding even the sharp weapons— Garuda, sword, bow, and arrows— which bore the marks of his own enemies,
he acts as the protector of his banner whose emblem is the tree-dweller (Hanumān).

O Incarnation of the Buddha, you who show compassion for those bound by poets, bestow your mercy upon me with palms joined; O bearer of the sword and shield that have achieved the destruction of the envious enemies of the Sugata, you who have mastered the Buddhist scriptures made accessible by the masters headed by Śauddhodani, and you whose vehicle is the pure horse Kamalā.
O Kalki by name, whose entire body is clearly bound with radiance, [enter] my inner sanctum! 32.

O you who wear the skin of a deer, O cloud-like bearer of water, O bestower of boons upon the king of deer; O you whose essence is struck by the mace, whose pride has vanished, whose strength of medicinal herbs has departed; O you who are like the essence of flowers in a deer, and whose pair of lotus-feet have reached the essence of the deer; O you who are the color of a fine deer, O remover of obstacles, O you whose pride in the lotus has vanished—speaking thus, protect me! 33.
May this work—the life story of which is delightful through its ten stages beginning with the birth of the egg-born [Brahmā] from the body struck by the arrow of his neck;

which is the abode of the playful speech of the King of Sages (Vyāsa), whose mind is exceedingly auspicious and noble; and which is the very dwelling for those who study it during the worship of Lord Hari, who is bowed to by the gods headed by Śrī Vāgadhīśa—become the residence for the multitude of worlds that are the abodes of the gods other than Vāgbhava (the Goddess of Speech).
